name: Tidio
task: Website or Shopify chat & FAQ deflection
summary: Live chat, ticketing and the Lyro AI agent in one platform: AI answers routine questions from your own data, hands the rest to the team with context, and Flows chase leads proactively. Lyro also plugs into Zendesk, Intercom, Salesforce and 20+ platforms without migration, but only on Premium.
best_for: support teams that want an AI agent and a help desk from one vendor and can size the shared conversation quota against their own volume, and Shopify, WordPress or Wix stores that want free live chat and treat the 50 free Lyro conversations as a test of whether the AI answers their questions
skip_if: you need the AI agent to keep answering past the first 50 conversations without paying, you are heading for Plus and cannot get its usage rate quoted before signing, you want one per-seat price rather than a conversation quota with metered add-ons, or you are buying on the strength of the 67 percent resolution figure and need it as a commitment rather than an average
honest_knock:
The AI number on the homepage and the AI number on the pricing page do not agree, and the pricing page is the lower of the two. The homepage, read 24 August 2026, says Lyro “resolves 67% of conversations instantly” and repeats it as a statistic: 67% of conversations resolved instantly. The pricing table, read the same day, lists “Guaranteed 50% Lyro AI resolution rate” as a Premium feature: the most expensive tier on the page. So the figure the marketing quotes is 17 points above the figure the company is willing to guarantee, and the guarantee is only available if you talk to sales about the top plan. Both numbers can be true at once; a typical result and a contractual floor are different things. But it does mean that if you are buying on the strength of 67 percent, you are buying an average someone else achieved, not a commitment to you.

Second, the plan table opens on annual billing and in the With Lyro AI mode. The headline $33 for Starter and $63 for Growth become $39 and $75 the moment you click Monthly, and the Human only toggle shows a different plan again: Starter at $29 with 100 conversations instead of 50. Nothing is hidden, and the annual column is honestly labelled “2 months free”, but the first number you see describes neither month-to-month billing nor a help desk without AI.

Third, “Free plan forever” is true for the help desk and not for the AI. Tidio's pricing FAQ, read 20 November 2026, says the Free plan's 50 human conversations and 100 Flows visitors renew every month, but its 50 Lyro AI conversations are a one-time quota that does not renew. The live chat and ticketing side keeps working at zero; the AI agent the homepage is built around stops after 50 conversations ever, which for a shop with any traffic is a matter of days. Read the free plan as a trial of Lyro inside a permanently free help desk, not as a free AI agent.

In our own test on 21 October 2026 Lyro answered ten of ten questions correctly from five answers we gave it, said it had no information on the two it could not know and offered 'Talk to a person', but it would not work out whether one month fell inside a 37-day warranty.

pricing.notes:
(read 20 November 2026 on www.tidio.com/pricing/, including its FAQ; this replaces the plan table we read on 24 August and 10 October 2026, which Tidio has since restructured) Every paid plan now comes in two modes, Human only and With Lyro AI, and Lyro is no longer sold as a separate add-on. Conversations handled by Lyro and by your team count toward one plan limit, and the same quotas (50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 750 or 1,000 conversations a month) apply in both modes. Paid month to month, Starter is $29 for 100 conversations Human only, or $39 for 50 conversations With Lyro AI. Growth Human only runs from $49 for 200 conversations to $199 for 1,000; Growth With Lyro AI runs from $75 for 100 conversations to $700 for 1,000. Annual billing gives 2 months free on Starter, Growth and the Flows, Inbox AI and Voice add-ons. The page opens on the annual column in the With Lyro AI mode, where Starter reads $33 a month billed $390 a year and Growth starts at $63 a month billed $750 a year. Starter and Growth both allow up to 10 agent seats and carry a 7-day free trial with no card. Plus starts at $300 a month plus monthly usage at “discounted usage rates” the page does not print; Premium is custom and is where the guaranteed 50% Lyro AI resolution rate and pay-per-resolution billing sit.

The Free plan includes 50 human conversations and 100 Flows visitors a month, plus a one-time quota of 50 Lyro AI conversations that does not renew. Add-ons are priced on their own: Flows by visitors reached, from $29 a month for 2,000 to $299 for 100,000; Inbox AI by the conversation quota of your plan, from $10 a month; Help Center at a flat $10 a month; No Tidio branding at a flat $20 a month; and Voice, enabled through sales in the US, Canada, Australia and the UK, from $19 a month for 20 calls to $349 for 1,000. There is no per-conversation overage price on Starter or Growth. If you switch on automatic upgrades at checkout, a limit that reaches 95% moves to the next tier and you pay that tier's price from then on; with them off, you raise the limit yourself.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the 7-day trial that starts with a new account, without a card: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We gave the Lyro AI agent five questions and answers about a made-up shop, asked it ten questions in the Playground, two it could not know, and changed one answer to see how fast it followed. The chat widget was not installed.
findings: Sign-up requires a website URL ('Can't be empty!'). Within minutes Tidio read 71 pages of the site we entered into Lyro's knowledge on its own. The source list can delete or set an audience in bulk, but excluding a source without deleting it is one source at a time. Before testing our five Q&As we deleted all 71 website sources Tidio had imported automatically, so the answers were checked against our test knowledge alone.
Usage and plan showed 'AI conversations 0/50' marked 'Lifetime quota' for Lyro. After 13 Playground questions it still read 0 / 50: Playground questions do not count.
A CSV with the columns Question and Answer was accepted as it was (5 Q&As).

Lyro answered nine of the ten fact and paraphrase questions fully. For the warranty question it repeated the correct 37-day term but did not determine whether one month fell within it. Each answer was marked 'AI response based on your data sources'.
Asked whether a fault after one month was covered by a 37-day warranty, Lyro gave the 37 days but said 'I'm not able to determine whether one month falls within that period'.
For the two questions our data did not answer (Sunday opening, return costs) it said it had no information and offered 'Talk to a person'; it made nothing up.
After we changed the warranty from 37 to 41 days, the next question was answered with 41 days.
